items.where: second storey (8.7-11.3 m) of both end pavilions: a standing female figure either side of the window, on the balustraded sill; the same pair flanks the corner window (w03)
items.how: per figure a plinth block, a tapered body box, a head disc and a capital block on the pier, in the shaded stone

items.where: window hoods: triangular pediments over the third-storey windows of the centre axes (15.4-16.9 m), a broken pediment with a cartouche over the middle axis, segmental pediments with a relief over both pavilion windows, triangular pediments over the second-storey pavilion windows
items.how: poly() pediments with a raking cornice strip and a cartouche block; segmental hoods as segBand

items.where: ground and mezzanine of the three centre axes (0.45-7.0 m): one dark-framed shop window two storeys tall, split by a dark transom band at 3.8-4.5 m into the shop glazing and the mezzanine glazing
north-west pavilion ground storey: dark wooden double door (1.7 x 3.4 m) under a carved segmental pediment with a cartouche (3.8-5.0 m), the mezzanine window above
middle axis, under the third-storey window (12.0-12.8 m): a projecting stone balcony with a pierced balustrade (round openings)
under both second-storey pavilion windows (8.2-8.7 m): stone balustrades between the figure plinths
crowning cornice over the whole front (19.3-21.3 m): a frieze, a dentil course and modillion brackets under the corona
pilaster stacks with panelled faces between the centre axes and banded piers at the pavilion edges, from the entablature to the frieze
items.how: stone strips with stacked panel blocks; pavilion edge piers banded every 0.6 m

items.where: on the roof behind the glazed storey, about 27.4-28.9 m: the word METZ in tall pale letters inside a semicircular steel frame

items.note: seen in the 2022 aimed view from the Keizersgracht and the 2025 face crop

walls.note: The Keizersgracht front (BAG ring vertex 3 to vertex 8, 15.6 m), read on the whole-face rectified crop of b_20250120_0926_Track25_Sphere_00005 (2025, 40 px/m, obliquity 7 deg) and the brief crop w01-224.alt.jpg (2022). The brief's primary 2017 crop looks at the underside of the Leidsestraat bridge from a boat and shows nothing of the building. Symmetric five-axis front: two 4.3 m end pavilions (the north-west one 0.5 m proud, BAG edge 5) round three centre axes; the north-west pavilion carries the entrance and an attic gable, the south-east pavilion runs into the corner tower. Heights from the 3DBAG cornice (21.3 m) and the 2025 crop (h = 2.44 + 0.02575 x (1162 - y)).

items.where: the whole Leidsestraat front: corner pavilion with the figure pair at the second storey, three centre axes over a two-storey dark shop window, the north-east entrance pavilion with a carved doorway and an attic gable, the cornice and the glazed roof storey
items.how: the Keizersgracht front scheme mirrored onto this front, centre axes respaced over the 0.7 m longer centre zone

items.where: north-east pavilion ground storey: carved doorway with a broken pediment and cartouche over a dark wooden door

walls.note: The Leidsestraat front (BAG ring vertex 11 to vertex 20, 16.35 m). The brief crop w02-143 is the red-brick corner building on the other side of the Leidsestraat (the panorama stands on the Keizersgracht quay south-east of the junction and looks through it): no evidence for this pand. Read instead from the oblique view up the Leidsestraat out of TMX7316010203-002860_pano_0000_000046 (2022, heading 252, pitch 31) and the right wing of the aimed corner view w03-175.thumb.jpg: the same storey lines and five axes as the Keizersgracht front, mirrored, with the entrance pavilion (0.36 m proud, BAG edge 19) at the north-east end and the corner pavilion at the chamfer.

items.where: on the corner tower: a lead-grey square-plan bell dome (31.6-36.2 m) with an oeil-de-boeuf lucarne on each face, an open columned lantern (36.2-38.3 m), a small cap dome, a ball and a spike (to about 40.4 m)
items.how: 4-sided lathe bell profile turned 45 deg, ring-and-disc lucarnes, 8 column cylinders under an entablature ring, cap lathe, sphere, cone

items.where: tower stage 27.5-31.6 m over the roof: a stone square with a white clock face on the west and east faces, plain panels on the south and north, balls on the corners of the ledge below, a moulded cornice
items.note: the west clock seen frontal from the Keizersgracht (2022) and on the left face from the Leidsestraat bridge (2023); the east clock is the symmetric counterpart

items.where: chamfer attic over the cornice (21.3-26.0 m): a semicircular pediment framing a carved relief over two small windows, scrolls at the sides, an entablature over it
items.how: archBand pediment, a stone relief block with a raised disc, two small lights, side scroll discs

items.where: fluted colossal columns either side of the third- and fourth-storey corner windows (12.9-19.3 m)
items.how: 12-sided cylinders with base and capital blocks

items.where: the bowed stone balcony on a basket corbel under the third-storey corner window (11.2-12.9 m) and the straight balustraded balcony under the fourth-storey window (15.7-16.8 m)

ground storey: tall wooden corner entrance with a transom of two lights (0.4-3.0 m), a white mezzanine panel over it (3.8-5.8 m), large carved consoles carrying the entablature, carved panels either side

walls.note: The 4.4 m chamfer on the corner, read on w03-175.jpg (2022, 50.45 px/m, obliquity 1 deg; heights h = (1393 - y)/50.45 fitted to the 3DBAG cornice 21.3 m) and the 2021 crop.
